title: Before and after: előtt and után

sections.title: Time with előtt and után
sections.content: You know *előtt* (before) and *után* (after) with meals and work. They follow the noun, which does not change: *Ebéd után sétálok.* (After lunch I go for a walk.) *Vacsora előtt olvasok.* (Before dinner I read.) The time phrase usually comes first and the verb has its normal present-tense ending.

sections.title: Days follow each other
sections.content: Use the same words for days: *Péntek után szombat van.* (After Friday comes Saturday.) *Kedd előtt hétfő van.* (Before Tuesday comes Monday.)

items.english: After lunch I go for a walk.

sections.content: Say the event, then the time word: *ebéd után*, never *után ebéd*. The event word does not take *-t*.
